title: Can Diamondbacks Realistically Land Skubal?

 Don Strouble Partner Nov 17, 2026 12:57 AM Published Nov 17, 2026 12:57 AM The Arizona Diamondbacks need to make moves in free agency that can make them a legitimate contender again. Could they have a shot at landing Tarik Skubal?
 As the days of November roll by and the holiday season grows closer, the stakes of the Major League Baseball offseason are starting to ramp up. The General Manager meetings took place in Las Vegas from Nov. 10-12, and some free agents have already begun to find new homes.
 Certain clubs have similarities concerning the needs they have to address this offseason, but ultimately, each path taken by an organization will be unique in its own way.
 For the Arizona Diamondbacks , it is largely about finding a way to meaningfully compete in the National League landscape once again. After winning the NL pennant in 2023, the Diamondbacks have gone on to post two winning seasons in the last three years. 
 However, that has not been good enough to get them back to the playoffs.
 Related stories
 Arizona's offense is mostly solid, but its pitching staff could use some work. Tarik Skubal is not only the best available pitcher in the free-agent market, but he is also the most sought-after free agent in general right now. 
 Whoever signs him is going to have to back up the Brinks truck for him. Is it realistic to think that the Diamondbacks could be a legitimate suitor for him?
 Perhaps it's possible for Diamondbacks
 Recently, ESPN MLB insider David Schoenfield grouped all 30 MLB teams into five tiers to demonstrate the likelihood of them landing Skubal. Tier five represented the teams that have no shot, and tier one represented the favorites. 
 Additionally, Schoenfield provided backup options for each club if they miss out on the two-time Cy Young Award winner.
 In Schoenfield's eyes, Arizona belonged in the second tier, which is considered to be the long shots. Schoenfield noted that the Diamondbacks have a history of signing coveted free agent pitchers to big contracts. 
 In 2016, Arizona made Zack Greinke the highest-paid pitcher with a $206 million deal. In December 2024, the Diamondbacks signed Corbin Burnes to a $210 million deal. 
 That's a lot of money wrapped up in two pitchers over the last decade, and Arizona only has its 2023 pennant to show for it.
 Additionally, owner Ken Kendrick made comments after the Diamondbacks' season ended in which he revealed his desire to trim payroll . A team on the verge of cutting costs usually isn't going to be the one to sign the top free agent of any class, let alone Skubal. 
 Still, there is always a chance Kendrick could reverse course, and the organization could shock the baseball world.
 If the Diamondbacks do not land Skubal, who else should be on their radar?
 The other options
 For Arizona, one such option is already in the building, and that is right-hander Michael Soroka . 
 According to Schoenfield, the Diamondbacks could explore re-signing Soroka in order to fill out the rotation. Foster Griffin, an All-Star lefty in 2026, could also bring value at a much smaller price tag. 
 Schoenfield highlighted that Griffin is projected to earn a two-year, $30 million contract, and Soroka is projected to earn a two-year, $24 million deal. These are much friendlier financial situations for Arizona to explore rather than giving all they have to one player.
